title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding
summary: LiLiCorr replaces raw block-parallel drafting (e.g., DFlash), whose per-position marginals produce jointly incoherent token blocks, with a lightweight head that scores adjacent candidate pairs via in/out vector cosine similarity and a greedy walk to select a coherent draft path. Costs include an extra network pass and batched pairwise scoring (about 2.8% of per-block latency), plus co-training the drafter with LiLiCorr, which adds a training step beyond simply deploying a pretrained drafter. It can fail if the reader does not already use a diffusion-style block drafter (the method presupposes one), if co-training is infeasible under the compute budget, or on workloads whose distributions differ from the training setup, since gains are acceptance-length dependent and workload-specific.
rationale: The technique is a low-overhead inference-time addition, but it presupposes a DFlash-style block drafter and a co-training stage, so the reader must validate acceptance-length gains on their own model and workload before adopting it in production.
technique: Likelihood-correlation scoring of block-parallel draft tokens

claims.statement: LiLiCorr replaces raw block-parallel drafting (e.g., DFlash), whose per-position marginals produce jointly incoherent token blocks, with a lightweight head that scores adjacent candidate pairs via in/out vector cosine similarity and a greedy walk to select a coherent draft path. Costs include an extra network pass and batched pairwise scoring (about 2.8% of per-block latency), plus co-training the drafter with LiLiCorr, which adds a training step beyond simply deploying a pretrained drafter. It can fail if the reader does not already use a diffusion-style block drafter (the method presupposes one), if co-training is infeasible under the compute budget, or on workloads whose distributions differ from the training setup, since gains are acceptance-length dependent and workload-specific.

Raises acceptance length by 9-19% over the vanilla DFlash drafter, with the scoring head accounting for about 2.8% of per-block latency; highest throughput in 70 of 72 benchmark settings against DFlash and two concurrent coherence-restoring methods.

equations.context: A natural formulation scores each full path by summing its matching terms across the block and selects the path that maximizes this whole-chain score. We argue that this is the wrong target for speculative decoding. The global optimum may sacrifice an early slot to win a richer tail, yet under prefix acceptance that tail is never reached. Section 3.5 and Appendix E take up this comparison at decoding time. Optimizing the whole chain thus spends capacity on regions the metric never credits. We therefore score each slot locally, conditioned on the candidate committed just before it. equations.context: Decoding has a parallel- and a sequential stage, and the network runs only once. In the parallel stage, a single LiLiCorr pass produces every outgoing and incoming vector, including the anchor out vector. The block has <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> adjacent slot pairs, and within each pair every candidate is matched against every candidate in the next slot.
